lawyer:
Akram Hossain Amin ----- For the petitioner.
B.N. Chowdhury ----- For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Esaruddin Mondal ----- Complainant petitioner.
Vs.
Abdus Sobhan Sarkar ----- Opp. Party.
full_judgment:
2. Complainant Esaruddin claimed to have possessed plot No. 1034 of mouza Kandura P. S. Puthia by inheritance from his father. In Badhra, 1373 B. S. he had grown kalai crop therein but on the 9th Aswin, corresponding to 26-9-66 the accused persons including accused Jaker started destroying the kalai crop by ploughing it up whereupon the complainant accompanied by his relations went to the land and protested against the ploughing. The accused persons who were variously armed with ballam, sup kis and falas attacked his party whereupon they left the kalai land and retreated to the adjacent land of one Solaiman but there they were surrounded by the accused persons one of whom namely Sobhan harled a fala from a short distance at palan hitting him right at the chest as a result of which, palan fell down and died instantaneously in Solaiman's land. Three other members of the complainant's party, Hamm, Bishu and Taller were also severely assaulted by the other accused with latis and surkis. The complainant immediately went to the thana and lodged a first Information Report where-upon a sub-Inspector of police came to the spot held inquest on the dead-body and forwarded it to the morgue for postmortem examination. He also seized sonic alamats including blood stained nara, a blood stained fala, some kalai crop etc. After investigating the case he challaned all the fifteen accused including accused Sobhan under various sections including section 302 and 148 of the Penal Code. A competent Magistrate of Rajshahi after holding a preliminary enquiry under chapter XVIII Cr. P.C. committed them to the court of session to stand their trial. Thus they were put on trial before the learned Sessions Judge on a common-charge under section 148 B.P. C. and another charge under sections 302/149 B.P.C. Accused Sobhan was further charged under section 302 B.P.C. for intentionally causing the death of palan. Three of the accused namely Tamiz, Jaher and Dulu were separately charged for causing simple hurts. They pleaded not guilty to the charges taking the cleffence that the land in question was in possession of accused Jaker who had got it by settlement. It is Jaker who had grown the kalai crop but when Jaker was working in the "kalai field" the complainant's party variously armed attacked Jaker in order to take forcible possession of the land and in that connection a free-fight took place between the parties which resulted in the fatal blow to palan, no body knowing at whose blow the complainant falsely implicated the accused out of enmity and grudge. The learned Sessions Judge on consideration of evidence of 15 witnesses for the prosecution and two witnesses for the defence acquitted all the accused from the various charges levelled against them. 

 3. The state did not file any appeal against the impugned order of acquittal. The rule in case was issued at the instance of the Complainant a private persons. 

 Mr. Akram Hossain Amin the learned Advocate appearing in support of the rule has referred to some observations of the learned trial Judge in his judgment and tried to show that the learned sessions Judge came to a palpably wrong finding due to serious misconception of law particularly law relating to the right of private defence of person and property. It appears that both the parties claimed possession of the land-plot No. 1034 by settlement from the same land lord one Hementa Kumer Sen about 20 years ago. In support of his settlement accused Jaker produced a deed of settlement records of right and some Rent-receipts, whereas no such documents were produced by the complainant who relied solely on oral evidence as to his possession by settlement. It appears that the learned Sessions Judge gave too much importance on the documentary evidence as to actual possession without giving any reason for rejecting the evil decree of the prosecution witnesses regarding actual possession of the land. P.W. 1 the complainant said that he had grown kalai crop in the land in the month of Bhadra but the accused persons started damaging it by ploughing on the day of occurrence i.e. on 9th Aswin. The defence suggestion is that the kalai crop was grown by accused Jaker and not by the complainant. The Investigating Officer P. W. 16, found damaged kalai crop in that land. According to P.W. 1 the kalai crop was being "destroyed by ploughing " but according to the defence the accused, owners of the land, were working there on that land on the relevant day. It is not understood what they meant by working on the kalai field particularly when the "Kalai" was not ripe for harvesting the incident taking place only within are month from the date of sowing Evidence of P.Ws. 1, 4, 5, 6 & 7 and others show that the kalai crop was being destroyed by the accused by ploughing. The Investigating Officer P.W. 16 seized some ploughs from the house of the accused. If the crop had been grown by the accused why they were ploughing it up ? The learned Sessions Judge did not at all direct his attention to this aspect of the matter. However he came to a finding that the accused were in possession of the land and "were working there" when they were attached by the complainant's party who wanted to take forcible possession. We are not inclined to interfere with this finding on fact but taking it as correct we examine whether the accused persons were protected by the right of private defence of property or of per-son or of both. 

 5. The Medical Officer (P.W. 2) has observed that the injury found in the dead-body "was slightly upward" from this learned Sessions Judge held that this injury could not be caused with a weapon "hurledj", the trend of the injury is dependent upon the distance as well as the angle from which the weapon is hurled. In the next breadth the learned judge observed" If the accused (Sobhan) hurled the Fala, he did not aim it at any particular person or at least he had no intention of causing death of anybody. It cannot be said by any stretch of imagination that accused Sobhan had the intention to cause the death of Palan so the charge under section 302 B.P.C. cannot stand. We cannot but express our surprise at this observation of the learned Sessions Judge who acted on a misconception of law that if a person kills another without any intention of causing death then no offence is committed "Culpable homicide" is committed by an act not only done with the intention of causing death but also with the knowledge that death is likely to be caused thereby. To hurl a fala at the chest of a person is certainly an act done either with the guilty intention or with the guilty knewledge as defined in law. Next, the learned Trial judge observed that the injury caused to Palan was not fatal, whereas, according to the Medical expert this injury was the cause of death. 

 6. Coming to the right of private defence of persons or property, it appears that the learned Sessions judge did not apply his mind at all to see what it is, what is its extent and where it begins and where it ends. According to the finding of the learned trial judge, the complainant's party had committed criminal trespass into the land of the accused who therefore had the right to resist. But this right does not extend to the causing death as specifically provided in section 104 of the Penal Code. This section provides that the right of private defence against criminal trespass extends to the causing of any hurt other than death. Again when the act of criminal trespass is discontinued, then there is no longer any necessity to exercise the right of private defence of property. In this case the actual assault upon Palan did not take place within the disputed plot but it took place on the adjacent land of Solaiman 90 yds. apart where Palan had retreated. 

 7. Now coming to the question of right of private defence of person, this question was not at all considered by the learned Sessions Judge who simply held that complaints party was responsible for the death of palan and that a maramari took place in which "both the parties were injured". On behalf of the defence two witnesses were examined and according to their defence one of the accused, namely Khudu received five injuries which were simple in nature these facts hardly constituted any apprehension of death or grievous hurts from the complainant's party, particularly when that party left the disputed land and retreated to land of Soleman, a third person. The right of private defence of person comes to an end as soon as the aggressors leave the scene of occurrence. To attack and surround the retreating persons is not an act protected by the right of private defence of person or property. The learned Sessions Judge is found to have tried the case on misconception of law defining "culpable homicide" and governing "the right of private defence" and thereby committed grave miscarriage of justice. 

 8. Mr. B.N. Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing to oppose the Rule has found it difficult to support some of the observations of the learned Trial Judge but he has contended that a mere illegality or misconception of law is not sufficient to warrant interference with an order of acquittal unless such interference is necessitated in the interest of state policy. We have hardly anything to differ with Mr. Chowdhury on this broad proposition of law. But the acquittal of at least, accused Sobhan which is based on erroneous view of law should in our opinion be interfered with in the interest of public order and "state policy". We are also aware that about nine years have elapsed since the incident and about seven years since the trial, but since a manifest illegality causing grave injustice is concerned, mere delay or lapse of time cannot be a ground for refusing interference in a case of acquittal. 

 In the circumstances we direct that accused Abdus Sobhan Sarker (opposite party No. 1 be retried on a charge under section 304 of the Penal Code. The Rule is made absolute only in the case of accused Abdus Sobhan Sarker and it is discharge in the case of the rest. The Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi is directed to rearrest accused Sobhan and produce him before the court for trial. Ho may also release the accused on bail if prayed for.
